Methods for inferrer objects

inferrer-methods.Rd

The objects returned by the infer_* functions support tidy(), which returns the inferences as a tibble with one row per candidate term, and print(), which summarizes them.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'inferrer'
tidy(x, scale_coef = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'inferrer'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

an inferrer

scale_coef

if TRUE (default), estimates are per standard deviation of each predictor; if FALSE, per unit. See "Scale of the coefficients".

...

additional parameters (not yet used)

Value

tidy() returns a tibble with one row per candidate term (plus the intercept):

  • term, selected, coef: as in tidy() for the selector (see tidy.selector()). coef is the selector's own estimate.

  • estimate: the inference method's estimate, which can differ from coef: a refit of the selected model for infer_upsi(), the selective-inference estimate for infer_selective(), and the mean over resamples for infer_boot().

  • ci_low, ci_high: the confidence interval at the inferrer's conf.level.

  • p_value: from infer_upsi(), infer_selective() and infer_pipe().

  • prop_selected: from infer_boot(), the proportion of resamples in which the term was selected.

  • null_radius: from infer_boot(), the padding radius (see its pad argument).

How non-selected terms are filled in depends on the method's nonselection (see infer_upsi()) or, for infer_boot(), inference_target.

print() returns, invisibly, a summary of the CI lengths.

Scale of the coefficients

Coefficients, estimates and intervals are on the same metric as the selector's; see "Scale of the coefficients" in tidy.selector(). By default (scale_coef = TRUE) they are per standard deviation of each design column; with scale_coef = FALSE they are per unit. The intercept is never unscaled.

Intervals and null_radius are converted along with the estimates.
